messages:
sara: Heads-up — after the microbatch bump to 8 for streaming chat we started seeing p99 tail spikes. Non-stream completions with mb=8 look fine. Anyone seen similar?

mike: Which model/hardware and workload? any profiling yet? :thinking:

dina: Quick run on a small replica (A100-p4d-ish): streaming mb=8 -> p50 78ms / p95 215ms / p99 480ms. Non-stream mb=8 -> p50 85ms / p95 180ms / p99 260ms. So tail growth mainly in streaming path.

eli: Observed KV cache eviction spikes during the streaming experiments. Evictions/sec jumps correlate with p99. If I disable prefix caching tails disappear. Could be cache sharding + interleaved microbatches.

jess: Config snippet we rolled out:
```
runtime.microbatch.size = 8
runtime.streaming.enabled = true
runtime.batching.window_ms = 50
runtime.kv.cache.policy = LRU
```

sara: Confirmed metrics: `kv_evictions: 120/s` at the p99 hotspots. Also saw more uneven token counts per microbatch in traces.

mike: Kernel note: streaming path uses the fused multihead kernel (opt-fused). It has better mean but worse tail variance when token counts are skewed across the batch. Switching to the fallback kernel reduced p99 by ~120ms but bumped mean ~+10ms. :warning:

dina: Profiling snapshot (short):
```
45% token_decode_kernel (fused)
18% kv_cache_lock_wait
12% network_enqueue
10% python overhead
5% other
```

eli: Two practical mitigations I can see: 1) reduce mbsize for streaming (8->6) to reduce tail, 2) enable kv_shard_affinity so streaming microbatches tend to reuse the same shard, or 3) add a small batching hold (30ms) to smooth token count variance.

jess: Proposed experiment matrix:
- modes: streaming vs non-stream
- mbsize: 4, 6, 8
- kernel: fused vs fallback
- kv_affinity: on/off
Run 5k reqs per cell, record p50/p95/p99 + evictions and kernel wait hist.

sara: I'll schedule the matrix tonight and start with streaming/modes first. Want clear p95/p99 deltas and tradeoff numbers so PMs can decide SLOs. @perf-bot can you kick off trace collection for this thread id?

perf-bot: Scheduled perf collection job id=pc-1832504321 for 2026-11-03T02:00:00Z. Artifacts will land in s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/pc-1832504321.

mike: Also flagging the kernel commit `abc123` from last week as a potential regression vector — try the matrix with that commit reverted too.

jess: Will wire a canary route: streaming requests -> mbsize=6, kernel=fallback, kv_affinity=on for 10% traffic so we can compare in prod without full rollout.

sara: Great. If canary looks good we'll keep mb=6 for streaming and mb=8 for non-stream. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
